name: Boston Electronics
old_description: SiC photodiode UV sensors and probes meet the demanding needs for lamp monitoring and control in water, air, sun, surface, curing and instrument applications.
about:
Boston Electronics operates from Brookline, Massachusetts. The company is a tradename of 49Chestnut LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company, and Fiber Optic Center, Inc., which acquired Boston Electronics Corporation in November 2025. For forty years it has served as a distributor of electro-optical solutions, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The firm distributes advanced electro-optical components and specialized systems for microscopy, offering a broad portfolio that includes UV sensors and probes (SiC photodiodes), UV LEDs (255–405 nm), infrared detectors and imaging arrays (InGaAs PIN/APD, InAsSb, T2SLS), terahertz sources and imagers (QCL-based), photon-counting modules (TCSPC/FLIM), quantum cascade lasers, and laboratory instrumentation such as blackbody sources and laser power meters. It provides knowledgeable application support to help customers select and integrate these technologies.

Customers span environmental monitoring, process control, scientific instrumentation, life sciences and biomedical technologies, building and home automation, security and surveillance, and microscopy. The company works with researchers and manufacturers developing products for water and air purification, curing, lidar, thermal imaging, and spectroscopy.

Boston Electronics positions itself as a specialist in photo-detection and photon generation, representing leading manufacturers worldwide—including Hamamatsu, Becker & Hickl, Alpes Lasers, and Gentec-EO—to bring advantaged, unique-performance solutions to a broad market. Its stated differentiator is close collaboration with customers to address sensor requirements across diverse applications.
